newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Dec 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Dec 26.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
Cities of Qingdao, Shenzhen, Ningbo and Dalian invest 183 million yuan in impoverished province of Guizhou.
Pictures of train named after chairman Mao Zedong, bronze statue of Great Helmsman and library and garden built in his memory to mark his birth anniversary.
Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin calls on authorities to look after retired military officers in their old age.
Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji calls for establishing modern, effective system to supervise and prevent loss of state assets.

Record year for new listings of companies on China's two stock markets, with a 1996 total of 201 listed as of December 25. Total listings now 524 with a total share capitalisation of nearly 110 billion yuan, of which 34 billion is tradeable.
Ban on sugar imports to remain in place in 1997.
State Planning Commission think tank forecasts economy to grow 10.5 percent in 1995 with inflation under 6.0 percent.
Britain urged not to create trouble in run-up to Hong Kong reverting to Chinese rule in mid-1997.
